# Review Home Base — First Principles Engine

> **What this is:** the single anchor for the Barnes homeschool app's architecture & functional review.
> **Where reviewing happens:** a dedicated Claude.ai chat (the "home base"). It owns the recurring
> audit, holds the live issue ledger, and spins out fix runs.
> **Where fixing happens:** Claude Code web, driven by the prompts in `prompts/`, reviewed before merge.
> **Repo:** github.com/barnes-ngb/first-principles-engine · **Live:** first-principles-engine.web.app
> **Created:** 2026-05-29 · **Last audit:** 2026-08-30 (`ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-30.md`; prior: August 23 mid-cycle audit `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-23.md`, August 16 mid-cycle audit `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-16.md`, August 9 mid-cycle re-verification `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08-09.md`, August 2 primary monthly run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-08.md`, July 26 run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-26.md`, July 19 primary run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-19.md`, July 12 mid-cycle re-verification `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07-12.md`, July 5 run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-07.md`, June 28 run `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-06-28.md`, June 21 mid-cycle supplement, primary June run: `ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_2026-06.md`)

---

## 1. Why this exists

The project already has a working maintenance system (Tiers 1–3 below) that keeps stats and docs
honest every few days. What it lacked was **teeth on architecture** and a path from *finding* to *fix*.
This home base adds that: one recurring deep audit focused on structure and the end-to-end loop, plus
a repeatable fix runner so issues don't just get logged — they get closed.

## 2. Review priority order

Set by Nathan, 2026-05-29. The audit and ledger weight findings in this order:

1. **Architecture & tech debt** — structure, decomposition, bundle, test coverage. *(primary)*
2. **Functional / UX completeness** — does the evaluate → plan → execute → review loop actually work for Shelly and the boys.
3. **Pedagogy & ethos alignment** — charter fidelity, disposition-over-mastery, no-shame, coverage-not-pace.
4. **Data integrity & compliance** — hours aggregation, MO 600-core line, source-of-truth conflicts.

> Note: an item in a lower band still jumps the queue if it is **time-sensitive or compliance-critical**
> (e.g. DATA-01 below, which affects the June 30 MO core-hours line).

## 3. How to run the home base

| Action | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Monthly deep audit** | Claude Code web (scheduled) | Run `prompts/PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md`. Same scheduling mechanism as your /3-day health audit. Suggested: 1st of month, after the health audit. |
| **Fix an issue** | Claude Code web (manual) | Run `prompts/PROMPT_FIX.md` with one issue ID from the ledger (§6). |
| **Strategy / triage / "should we even do this"** | Claude.ai home-base chat | Paste this file + the latest dated audit report. Talk it through. Decisions land back in the ledger. |
| **Refresh project context** | Claude.ai project settings | Point the project at `docs/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (regenerated weekly by Tier 3), not the stale v14 outline. See DOC-01. |

## 4. The existing maintenance system (unchanged — for reference)

| Tier | Cadence | Output | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 — Health Audit** | every 3 days | `docs/HEALTH_REPORT.md` (stats, build/lint/test, doc drift, auto-fixes numbers) | Claude Code scheduled |
| **2 — Fix Companion** | after Tier 1 | auto-fixes mechanical doc gaps (undocumented tasks, missing collections, nav, index) | Claude Code scheduled |
| **3 — Context Gather** | weekly | `docs/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` (AI-optimized context for design chats) | Claude Code scheduled |
| **4 — Deep Audit** | **monthly (this system)** | dated `docs/review/ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_<YYYY-MM>.md` + ledger update | Home base → Claude Code |

Tiers 1–3 stay as they are. This home base **is** Tier 4, made concrete.

## 5. Architecture map (as of 2026-05-29)

**Stack:** React + TypeScript + Vite · Firebase (Auth/Firestore/Storage/Functions/Hosting) · MUI ·
Three.js r128 (3D avatar) · Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 4.6 primary, Haiku 4.5 for routine chat) ·
OpenAI gpt-image-1.5 (image generation — migrated from DALL-E 3 + gpt-image-1 per PR #1217).

**Scale (verified against code 2026-06-20):** ~180,429 TS lines · 117 commits on main ·
37 Firestore collections · 25 Cloud Functions · 19 chat task types · 34 routes · 181 test files ·
2,746 tests passing · build/lint/tsc all green.

**The core loop (this is what "functional review" traces):**

```
Evaluate ──► Skill Snapshot ──► Plan My Week ──► Daily checklist (Today) ──► Weekly Review
   ▲              (priority skills,                  (evidence: completion,        │
   │               supports, stop rules,             engagement, mastery,         │
   └───────────────conceptual blocks)                minutes, artifacts) ─────────┘
```

**AI pipeline:** 17 task types dispatched via `functions/src/ai/tasks/` registry; per-task context
slices in `functions/src/ai/contextSlices.ts`; charter preamble injected into all calls.

**Feature homes:** `today/` · `planner-chat/` · `quest/` (Knowledge Mine) · `avatar/` (Hero Hub) ·
`books/` · `workshop/` · `shelly-chat/` (Ask AI) · `evaluate/` · `records/` · `dad-lab/` · `progress/`.

**The central architecture tension (already named in `first-principles-system-review.md`):**
the system can answer *"where is Lincoln right now?"* from **six** places — Skill Snapshot, Ladders,
Milestones, Learning Map, Curriculum position, Disposition profile — and **none is authoritative**.
The loop isn't missing; it has too many overlapping truths. Sharpening that authority is the single
highest-leverage architecture move. Tracked as **FUNC-01**.

## 6. Live issue ledger

Status: `OPEN` · `IN PROGRESS` · `FIXED` · `WONTFIX` · `NEEDS-DATA` (requires live Firestore export).
Band = priority band from §2. The audit prompt updates this table; the fix prompt flips status.

**Lanes (ID-prefix legend):** **Structure** — `ARCH` / `TEST` / `LINT` · **Functionality** — `FEAT` / `FUNC` · **Docs** — `DOC` / `ETHOS` · **Data/compliance** — `DATA`.

> **Before appending a row, re-fetch the ledger from `origin/main` and use `max(id)+1` per lane** — concurrent chats can't see each other's pending rows (see the ARCH-18 dup reconciled 2026-06-07, and the bulk dedup of 2026-06-08).

> **Only one ledger-touching run should be in flight at a time across all chats.** Merge it before dispatching the next — `max(id)+1` only protects *sequential* writes; parallel cross-chat appends still collide on the shared counter (the root cause of every duplicate ID swept so far).

> **The avatar / Hero Hub lane uses a distinct `AV-` ID prefix** (`AV-NN`) for its rows going forward, so its appends can't collide with home-base `ARCH-NN`. (Convention for future rows only — existing avatar rows keep their `ARCH-` IDs.)

> **London-specific work lives in `docs/LONDON_BACKLOG.md`, not as `FEAT-` rows.** Per the Lincoln-first /
> London-minimal policy (`CLAUDE.md` › AI Development Operating Model), London touchpoints are tracked
> surface-by-surface in that register to keep this active ledger Lincoln-focused.

No Firestore reconnect helper existed. **(0.4 — the class)** the planner generation path is the **outlier** — learner synthesis, weekly review, monthly review publish/republish, and photo vision extraction already wrap their long awaits in try/catch and are safe; only the planner reached the boundary (its persistence write was fire-and-forget). **The fix (protects the class, not just one call site):** **(1)** new pure `src/core/firebase/transientRetry.ts` — `isTransientConnectivityError` (Firestore `unavailable`/`deadline-exceeded` + offline/"could not reach backend" message text; **false** for `permission-denied`/`not-found`/`invalid-argument`/bad-data), `withTransientRetry(work, {attempts=3, baseDelayMs=300, sleep, onRetry})` (transient → exponential-backoff retry; genuine → rethrow **immediately**; exhausted → one honest **named** `TransientConnectivityError`; success path unchanged). Lives in `core` so it's outside the DOC-09 `src/features` scan. **(2)** planner path — `persistConversation`'s `getDoc` wrapped in `withTransientRetry`; a `TransientConnectivityError` is caught, logged at **warn**, and swallowed with an honest non-crashing notice ("You went offline — your draft is safe here and will sync when you reconnect"), while **genuine faults rethrow** (boundary behavior unchanged). **(3)** foreground retry — `ErrorBoundary` now classifies both entry points (`getDerivedStateFromError` + the `unhandledrejection` handler): a transient error shows a gentle **"Reconnecting…"** state (not the crash screen), and a `visibilitychange → visible` listener **auto-clears** it on return to the foreground (children re-render, the recovered draft is still in client state); genuine errors keep the full "Something went wrong" crash and do **not** auto-clear. **Recovery win:** returning to the tab clears the transient boundary and the completed draft is waiting (client state survives because the page no longer reloads; the last successfully-persisted draft also reloads from `plannerConversations`). **Class coverage:** the shared helper + the `ErrorBoundary` net protect every flow; only the planner call-site is wired this slice — **follow-ups** (belt-and-suspenders, all already try/catch-guarded today so none currently crash): route synthesis / weekly-review / monthly-review / photo-extraction reads through `withTransientRetry` for honest named exhaustion instead of silent snacks. **DOC-09:** the census is **unchanged** (8 remote-guard · 1 image-downscale · 93 silent catch(es)) — the helper is in `core` (unscanned), and the new planner `catch` rethrows genuine + logs warn, so it is not a silent catch. **Verify:** `tsc -b` clean; full suite green (**4181**, +12 = `transientRetry` +8, `ErrorBoundary` +4: unavailable retries→succeeds on attempt 2 without reaching the boundary, exhausted→named error, foreground `visibilitychange`→retry, `permission-denied`/`not-found`→escalate immediately, success-path characterization); lint clean; `docs:check` HARD green. Thin commits: (1) transient helper + tests, (2) planner path, (3) foreground retry + tests, (4) ledger. Refs **FEAT-61** (timeout/honest-error pattern). **Codex review (P1 + P2, both fixed):** **(P1, PlannerChatPage)** the transient-exhaustion branch *told* the user the draft "will sync" but dropped the failed update with no retry path — so a reload/eviction before another planner action lost it. Fix: on exhaustion, instead of dropping, issue a `setDoc(ref, {...updates, updatedAt}, {merge:true})` — a WRITE enters the Firestore SDK's in-memory mutation queue (reads don't) and flushes on the next same-session reconnect, so the "will sync" notice now holds (surviving a hard reload/eviction before reconnect stays the deferred durable-draft work; the draft also lives in React state meanwhile). **(P2, ErrorBoundary)** the transient auto-clear relied *solely* on a future `visibilitychange`, so a blip recorded while the tab was already visible (or a queued rejection drained after the foreground transition) never cleared. Fix: added a `window` **`online`** reconnect listener (clears a transient boundary the moment connectivity returns, any visibility) **plus** a 4s fallback self-heal timer (cleared on retry/unmount) so a transient state always clears even if `navigator.onLine` never flips — three independent recovery signals now. Tests +2 (online clears a transient already-visible blip; online does NOT clear a genuine error). | **FUNC-10** | 2 | **FIXED** | **Chapter-question generation no longer writes `chapterTitle: undefined` for untitled chapters (shared `buildChapterPoolItem`; fixes `setDoc` invalid-argument on Prince Caspian et al. across TodayPage/DevAdminTab/PlannerChatPage).** Generating chapter questions for any book added without per-chapter titles (e.g. Prince Caspian, 15 untitled chapters) failed on every entry point with `FirebaseError: [code=invalid-argument]: setDoc() called with invalid data. Unsupported field value: undefined`. **Root cause:** three duplicated create paths each mapped pool items with `chapterTitle: <chapter>?.title`, which is `undefined` for untitled chapters; the app's Firestore is plain `getFirestore(app)` (no `ignoreUndefinedProperties`), so a `chapterTitle: undefined` inside a `questionPool` item makes `setDoc` reject the whole `BookProgress` doc. `chapterTitle` was the only offender — the top-level `BookProgress` literals correctly omit their optionals. **Fix:** one shared `buildChapterPoolItem(q, chapterTitle?)` in `chapterPool.logic.ts` that **omits `chapterTitle` entirely** when there's no title (spreads `...(chapterTitle ? { chapterTitle } : {})`, never `undefined`) and returns `null` for malformed questions (missing/empty `questionType`/`question`) so callers `.filter(...)` them out. All three sites (`TodayPage.tsx`, `DevAdminTab.tsx`, `PlannerChatPage.tsx`) now map through it — same questions, same write, same `BookProgress` shape; titled books still carry titles onto pool items. Existing/already-answered pools untouched (create-mapping only). **Behavior-verified:** Prince Caspian (15 untitled chapters) → Generate chapter questions (Today + Settings dev) succeeds, pool fills 15/15, no Firestore error. No `ignoreUndefinedProperties` flip (deliberately out of scope — would mask real bugs app-wide). Branch `claude/pensive-dirac-4wj1yk`. | `src/features/today/chapterPool.logic.ts` (+`buildChapterPoolItem`/`RawChapterQuestion`, +4 tests in `chapterPool.logic.test.ts`), `src/features/today/TodayPage.tsx`, `src/features/settings/DevAdminTab.tsx`, `src/features/planner-chat/PlannerChatPage.tsx` |
| **FUNC-11** | 2 | **FIXED** | **`openChatWithContext` no longer writes `context.weekTheme`/`context.itemTitle: undefined` (omits absent fields); fixes the Today "Find a video" button crash (`addDoc` invalid-argument).** Tapping **Find a video** on a Today plan item threw `FirebaseError: [code=invalid-argument]: Function addDoc() called with invalid data. Unsupported field value: undefined (found in field context.weekTheme ...)`. **Root cause (same `undefined`-field class as FUNC-10, different write path):** `handleFindVideo` (`TodayChecklist.tsx`) calls `openChatWithContext(...)` **without** a `weekTheme`; `openChatWithContext` then wrote the thread's nested `context` object as `{ source, itemTitle, weekTheme }`, so `weekTheme: undefined` (and `itemTitle: undefined` for callers that omit it) landed in the `addDoc` and plain Firestore (`getFirestore(app)`, no `ignoreUndefinedProperties`) rejected the whole write. **Fix:** build the nested `context` so absent fields are **omitted, not written** (`source` always; `...(context.itemTitle ? { itemTitle } : {})`; `...(context.weekTheme ? { weekTheme } : {})`). Top-level thread fields are safe (`title`/`lastMessagePreview` already fall back to `initialMessage`; `chatContext` required; message `addDoc.content` always present). Superset spread — defined fields still written exactly as before, so other `openChatWithContext` callers are unchanged. **Behavior-verified:** with no week theme set, **Find a video** on an academic plan item opens Shelly's chat on a new thread seeded with the `"Find a short, kid-friendly video to help teach: …"` question, no Firestore error, seeded message present. No `ignoreUndefinedProperties` flip (out of scope — 3rd undefined-field bug, separate owner decision). Branch `claude/wizardly-brown-tfk5eg`. | `src/features/shelly-chat/openChatWithContext.ts` |

| **DATA-10** | 2 | **FIXED** | **Enable `ignoreUndefinedProperties` on client Firestore init — retires the undefined-write rejection class app-wide (writes omit undefined fields instead of throwing).** We hit this bug class 4× recently (FUNC-10 `chapterTitle`, FUNC-11 `weekTheme`/`itemTitle`, the latent video-logger `subjectBucket`), each needing its own conditional-spread guard. **Root cause of the class:** the single client Firestore init was plain `getFirestore(app)`, so any `setDoc`/`addDoc` carrying an `undefined`-valued field threw `FirebaseError [invalid-argument]` and rejected the whole write. **Fix (one line):** `src/core/firebase/firestore.ts` now inits via `initializeFirestore(app, { ignoreUndefinedProperties: true })` (confirmed the **single** client init — `initializeFirestore` is the first Firestore call; nothing else calls `getFirestore` in `src/`). Client writes with `undefined`-valued fields now **silently omit** those fields instead of throwing — the desired outcome for the optional fields all known instances involved. Existing defensive guards (`buildChapterPoolItem` conditional spread, `openChatWithContext`'s, the video logger's `subjectBucket`) **left in place** — redundant now but harmless and self-documenting. **Out of scope (hard):** the `functions/` Admin SDK side — `getFirestore()` is called locally across many task files with no central init and Admin `.settings({...})` can only be set once before first use, so it needs its own careful refactor; every bug instance was client-side. **Verified:** `tsc -b`, build, vitest (2674 ✓), lint clean (0 errors). Run SOLO. | `src/core/firebase/firestore.ts` (one edit: `getFirestore`→`initializeFirestore` import + init) |

| **TEST-05** | 1 | **FIXED (landed on `main` via PR #1621, 2026-07-25)** — this row is the incident record | **`origin/main`'s type check went red, which silently skipped every branch's tests in CI.** `npx tsc -b` failed on a clean checkout of `main` with exactly three errors, all in test files: `src/features/monthly-review/photoRefs.test.ts` (6,32) + (7,35) `TS2353` — two `PhotoRef` fixtures written as `{ url, caption }`, a shape `PhotoRef` has never had (the real type in `src/core/types/monthlyReview.ts` requires `id`/`storagePath`/`source`/`sourceDocId`/`capturedAt`) — and `src/features/quest/questModelSync.test.ts` (9,40) `TS2556` — `const mockDoc = vi.fn(() => ...)` infers a **zero-parameter** call signature, so the `doc: (...args: unknown[]) => mockDoc(...args)` spread three lines below had no rest parameter to land in (`mockGetDoc`/`mockSetDoc` are bare `vi.fn()` and accept anything, which is why only line 9 errored). **The blast radius is the point, and is the reason this row exists:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test` job runs Lint → Type check → Run tests **in that order**, so a failing type check makes Actions skip the "Run tests" step entirely. Every PR in flight showed a red `test` job it did not cause, and **no branch's tests actually executed in CI** for as long as this sat on `main` — a green-looking suite that was not running. CI on `main`'s own tip (`66a987c`) is a recorded `failure`, confirming it was `main`'s breakage and not any branch's. **Why it survived:** both files pass at *runtime*, so a green local `npm test` never surfaces it; only `tsc` sees it. An incremental `tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo` cache can also mask it locally — delete it to reproduce. **How it was fixed:** the repair landed on `main` in **PR #1621** (commit `21002a2`), which carried the same two-file fix as a prerequisite commit so its own branch could go green — reshaping the `photoRefs` fixtures to the real `PhotoRef` type via a `photo(id)` factory, and typing the `questModelSync` mock variadic (`vi.fn((...args: unknown[]) => { void args; … })`). A follow-up worth considering: run the type check and the tests as independent jobs (or `continue-on-error` the ordering) so a type failure can never masquerade as, or suppress, a test result. | `src/features/monthly-review/photoRefs.test.ts`, `src/features/quest/questModelSync.test.ts` (both fixed on `main` via #1621); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (step ordering — the follow-up, not changed) |

Because it is a near- and not a literal collapse, the **required pairwise-inequality test passes on `main` too** — it ships as a regression guard, and the behavioural tests are the fail-pre-fix ones. **Fix 1 (cleanup, local/free/instant — no AI call added):** four pure helpers. (a) **Sample inside the crop, not the photo** — `sampleBorderRgb` gains an optional `region` + `insetFraction` so the ring never starts on the outermost pixels; crop path 4%, "use whole image" 8% (`DEFAULT_`/`WHOLE_IMAGE_BORDER_INSET_FRACTION`). (b) **Sample the paper, not the scene** — `pickBackgroundSample` splits the ring's luminance into two clusters (1-D 2-means, deterministic min/max seeding) and, when separated **and** both hold ≥15% of the ring, prefers the **lighter** cluster, unless the darker one is decisively flatter (rescues dark construction paper on a bright rug); rule stated in a comment. **Why the photo failed:** the old plain median of the whole ring landed *between* paper and carpet — the wrong colour for either, so the paper survived opaque — and the whole ring's std dev tripped the `maxBackgroundStdDev` gate (35) into the weak HSL fallback. Feeding the gate the **chosen cluster's own** std dev is what unblocks it; both halves asserted on the carpet fixture. (c) **Drop the specks** — `removeSmallIslands`, connected-component pass whose bound (`computeMinIslandPixels`) is the **lower** of a frame fraction and a fraction of the largest island, so it tracks the drawing and not the camera's megapixels; **the largest island is always kept** whatever the threshold says (a drawing is legitimately several strokes apart). (d) **Let the graphite live** — `boostInkContrast` pushes surviving ink away from the background luminance, hue preserved by scaling all three channels together. **The regression rail is structural, not a tuning hope:** the gain tapers to exactly 1.0 and **skips pixels already ≥`fullRange` (120) from the background**, so marker — far from the paper by construction — is **byte-identical**, asserted as such. ORIGINAL never modified; every knob overridable via `CleanSketchOptions` with the current values as documented fallbacks (`borderSampleSize` 20 / `tolerance` 60 / `featherMultiplier` 1.5 / `edgeSoftness` 1 / `maxBackgroundStdDev` 35 all unchanged). **Fix 2 (styles):** each look names its own **palette, line weight and shading** via a `VisualRecipe` table; a theme picked **without** an explicit base style now **owns the whole look** rather than inheriting the watercolor sentence (that inheritance is what made the nine options converge), while an explicitly named style keeps both blocks so the book reimagine path (`useBackgroundReimagine`, always names a style) is unchanged in shape; the homogenising tail becomes an explicit do-not-drift instruction. **Option ids and the default are untouched so saved stickers do not re-map**; `fancyStyleLabel` lifted out of `DrawingGroupCard` so the library's version chips + aria-labels read from the same table the picker does. No change to the save/group-key model, no new paid call per drawing, no kid-facing copy beyond the style labels. **Verified pre-fix** by restoring the three source files from `origin/main` and re-running: every new behavioural assertion fails (`5 failed | 18 passed` on the prompt suite; the whole FEAT-158 cleanup block red). Reproduced with a probe before changing anything; the darker cluster now wins only when the lighter one is *actually busy* (`stdDev > minNoisyStdDev`, default 10) **and** the darker is materially flatter (strict `<`). *P2:* the dust bound scaled with the **camera**, not the drawing — 0.0002 of a 4000×3000 photo is 2,400 px, enough to erase an eye dot, a period or the dot of an "i"; rebuilt as `computeMinIslandPixels` (lower of 0.00002 of frame and 0.0005 of the largest island, resolved after labelling via a callback), an order of magnitude safer and tighter still for a sparse drawing. The hat is big. Sam can hop."*), which also replaces the by-age sample page inside the OUTPUT JSON schema; and **stated PRECEDENCE** over THEME GUIDANCE's `VOCABULARY STYLE`, over the sight-word slice's planner framing, and over *"Contractions are fine"* (**no contractions at Level ≤4**). The old RULES line becomes a pointer to the block — two statements of one constraint, one vague and one concrete, is how the vague one wins. **`sentenceTargetFor({ phonicsLevel, age })`** replaces `sentenceTargetForAge` at all three call sites: **L1-2 → 1-2 sentences (3-6 words); L3-4 → 2-3 (4-8); L5-6 → 2-3 (6-10); L7-8 → 2-4 (8-14)**, monotone non-decreasing, L1-2 shorter than the old ≤7 row; **age is the fallback only** (`sentenceTargetForAge` is kept and still exported for it). The fix is adopted only if it **parsed**, kept the **same page count**, and has **strictly fewer** hard words (`shouldKeepFixedStory`, pure); a tie or a throw keeps the original, so a bad fix can never cost the parent the story they already have. **Never a loop.** The response gains `readability { phonicsLevel, levelSource, passed, hardWords[], revised }` next to `stopReason`; `stopReason` deliberately stays the GENERATION's. Both calls are billed to `aiUsage`; the log line carries `readabilityLevel=N readability=pass|fail hard=N revised=yes|no`. Cost ceiling: **at most one extra call per generation**, at the same `maxTokensForPageCount` budget. **Part 4, the honest line.** `storyDraftMessage` gains `storyReadabilityClause`: *"— 2 words may be above London's level: castle, ready."*, plus *"(estimated from age — set London's phonics level under Working Levels on the Skill Snapshot for a better fit)"* when `levelSource === 'age'`. De-duped, capped at 6 named words then counted, singular/plural correct, appended as a new sentence when the line already closed one and as an em-dash clause when it did not — so **every pre-FEAT-176 line is byte-identical**. Plain and blameless (it reports on the STORY, never on the child), no error styling, **no new UI**: the parent fixes it in the revise chat they already have. *Rails held:* the pure module has no I/O and is **not** moved to `shared/` (the client only reads the returned `readability` field); no change to page count, the token budget, FEAT-169's three failure messages, the style/theme image path (FEAT-169/172/173/174) or the sight-word channel (`resolveStoryWords` untouched, typed words still win); read-only on `sightWordProgress` / `wordProgress` / `skillSnapshots` and **nothing writes a level** (`resolveStoryReadingLevel` gained one additive `phonics: number | null` field instead of re-parsing its text); not name-gated (nothing reads `isLincoln` or a child's name); nothing near hours / XP / diamonds / compliance / `firestore.rules` / the art quota. the fix prompt gets the complete story; the return is re-serialized from the new pure `mergeFixedStory` (fixed fields win, only absent keys restored, `pages` never restored) so a model that quietly omits a field cannot reach the client. **P2: a denser fix could win on a technicality.** `shouldKeepFixedStory` compared only `totalHardWords` (the sum of per-page DISTINCT counts), so trading three distinct above-level words for one repeated a dozen times scored "better" while reading worse. ## 7. Triggers (phone-first cheat-sheet)

Everything below is either fully automatic or a single short message pasted into Claude Code web.
No local commands, ever.

### Fully automatic (set once)
- **Monthly audit** — scheduled Claude Code task, same as the /3-day health audit. Task prompt:
  > Read `docs/review/prompts/PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md` and execute it fully.

  Suggested schedule: 1st of the month, after the health audit. It auto-applies safe doc fixes and
  opens a PR for everything else. You just review + merge from the phone.

### One-line triggers (paste into Claude Code web on the repo)
- **Run a fix** (you pick the issue ID from §6):
  > Read `docs/review/prompts/PROMPT_FIX.md` and run it for ISSUE_ID: DATA-01

- **Run the audit now** (off-schedule, e.g. before a design session):
  > Read `docs/review/prompts/PROMPT_ARCH_AUDIT.md` and execute it fully.

- **Just triage / ask** (in the Claude.ai home-base chat, not Claude Code):
  > Read REVIEW_HOME_BASE.md and the latest audit report. What should I fix next and why?

### What is and isn't automated (by design)
- **Auto, no touch:** the audit, stat/doc corrections, PR creation.
- **One tap from you:** merging any PR.
- **Deliberately manual:** fixes that change real code or data — compliance hours, XP ledger, charter
  preamble. These propose-and-stop so a human decides. That's a safety feature for a system holding a
  child's school records, not a gap to close.



## 8. Conventions for this system

- **Design here, build there.** This home base produces decisions and prompts. Claude Code makes the code changes, always on a branch, always reviewed before merge.
- **Inspect → validate → propose for anything touching an invariant.** Hours math, XP ledger, and the additive-hours rule are never auto-fixed. They land as a proposal in the ledger for a human call.
- **One issue ID per fix run.** Keeps PRs small and reviewable.
- **Ledger is the memory.** If it isn't in the ledger, it didn't happen. Every audit and fix updates it.
- **Environment is Claude Code web, phone-first.** Nathan rarely runs anything locally. Claude Code web executes all builds/lint/tests/git in its own environment as part of running a prompt. No prompt should ask the human to run a command, install tooling, or use a local shell. The human's actions are limited to: pasting a prompt, uploading files, and reviewing/merging PRs from the phone.
